title: Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand
description: Manually move freight, stock, luggage, or other materials, or perform other general labor. Includes all manual laborers not elsewhere classified.

tasks.text: Maintain equipment storage areas to ensure that inventory is protected.
Read work orders or receive oral instructions to determine work assignments or material or equipment needs.
Move freight, stock, or other materials to and from storage or production areas, loading docks, delivery vehicles, ships, or containers, by hand or using trucks, tractors, or other equipment.
Install protective devices, such as bracing, padding, or strapping, to prevent shifting or damage to items being transported.
Sort cargo before loading and unloading.
Attach identifying tags to containers or mark them with identifying information.
Record numbers of units handled or moved, using daily production sheets or work tickets.
Attach slings, hooks, or other devices to lift cargo and guide loads.
Carry needed tools or supplies from storage or trucks and return them after use.
Pack containers and re-pack damaged containers.
Assemble product containers or crates, using hand tools and precut lumber.
Adjust controls to guide, position, or move equipment, such as cranes, booms, or cameras.
Connect electrical equipment to power sources so that it can be tested before use.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
skills.def: Software to manage, monitor, or optimize the flow of goods or services from an origin point to a destination. Examples: Warehouse management system WMS.

skills.name: Internet browser software
skills.def: Software to view the contents of web pages and to navigate from one page to another. Examples: Apple Safari, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Google Docs, Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Data entry software, Oracle Database.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: IBM Notes, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD.
